title: Computers
subtitle: log in, back up, hard drive
summary: Name the parts of a computer and talk about logging in, saving, backing up and installing software.

lesson.heading: Parts of a computer
rows: **screen**
the flat part you look at
**keyboard**
the part with the letters and numbers that you type on
**spacebar**
the long key at the bottom of the keyboard that makes a space
**escape key**
the key at the top left that stops what you are doing
**mouse**
the small thing you move with your hand to control the screen
**mouse mat**
the flat square that the mouse sits on
**printer**
the machine that puts your document on paper
**webcam**
the little camera that lets other people see you
**microphone**
the part that picks up your voice
**memory stick**
a small thing you put into the computer to carry files
**CD-ROM**
a disc that holds information you can read on a computer

lesson.heading: Starting work
lesson.text: First you **switch on** your computer. Then you may need to **log in** (or **log on**) with your **username** and **enter your password**. Your password is a special word that only you know. If you **double-click** on an **icon**, a small picture on the screen, you **open an application** such as email or an Internet browser.

examples.text: I **switched on** the computer and waited.
You can't **log in** without a **username** and a **password**.
**Double-click** on the **icon** to open the program.
When you finish, don't forget to **log out**.
examples.note: or log off; opposite of log in

lesson.heading: Storing and backing up
lesson.text: Computers can **store** large amounts of information. But while you are working it is important to **back up** your files. That means you make an extra copy of them, called a **backup**. Then you do not lose your work if something goes wrong.

examples.text: This computer can **store** thousands of photos.
I **back up** my files at the end of every day.
The data is on the hard disk, but I always make a **backup**.

lesson.heading: Working with documents
lesson.text: To **create** a new document, select *new* from the **File menu**. You can **copy and paste** information from one file into another, or **cut** it if you want to remove it. If you **save** the document, you can **print it out** later. The paper copy is a **hard copy** or a **printout**.

examples.text: **Create** a new document and give it a name.
I **copied** the address and **pasted** it into my email.
**Save** the document in case the computer **crashes**.

lesson.heading: Questions people ask about computers
rows: Do you have a **PC** or a **laptop**?
PC is short for personal computer; a laptop is a small computer you can carry around
What **hard drive** do you have?
the part inside the computer that stores large amounts of information; also called the hard disk
What **operating system** are you using?
the software, e.g. Windows or Mac OS, that controls how the computer works
Have you **installed** any new **software**?
install = put new programs onto your computer
Do you have **anti-virus software**?
a **virus** is a program put on a computer to destroy or steal information; anti-virus software stops it getting in

lesson.text: We log in **to** a computer but back up files - and the noun is written as one word: make a **backup**.

exercises.prompt: Match the word on the left with the word that goes with it.
A small computer that you can carry round with you is a ___.
exercises.explanation: A laptop is a small computer you can carry around.

exercises.prompt: The special word you type into your computer that only you know is your ___.
exercises.explanation: You enter your password when you log in.

exercises.prompt: Computer software that controls how the different parts work together is the ___.
exercises.explanation: Windows and Mac OS are operating systems.

exercises.prompt: The part inside the computer that stores large amounts of information is the hard ___.
exercises.explanation: The hard drive, also called the hard disk, stores the information.

exercises.prompt: A program secretly put on a computer to destroy the information on it is a ___.
exercises.explanation: A virus destroys or steals the information on a computer.

exercises.prompt: *A:* How often do you ___ your files? *B:* At the end of every day if I can remember.
exercises.explanation: Back up = make an extra copy of your files.

exercises.prompt: *A:* Did you ___ the software yourself? *B:* No, I don't understand anything about computers. My wife did it for me.
exercises.explanation: Install = put new programs onto your computer.

exercises.prompt: *A:* How do I create a new document? *B:* Just select new from the File ___.
exercises.explanation: You start a new document from the File menu.

exercises.statement: If you want to stop using an application, you can press the escape key to exit.
exercises.explanation: Correct. Exit means stop using an application.

exercises.statement: When your computer suddenly stops working, we say it saves.
exercises.explanation: When your computer suddenly stops working, we say it crashes.

exercises.prompt: Do you do these things at the start of your work, or with a document?
Ask about the programs someone has put on their computer.
exercises.answer: Have you installed any new software?
exercises.explanation: Install software = put new programs onto your computer.
